observations: Genuine queued model requests retain background/foreground intent; foreground takes the next turn, model turns serialize and a CPU lane remains available. Native model launcher held.
Foreground activity expires without changing an assignment; pressure defers admission. Owner queue promotion changes admission priority independently of CPU nice.
A 32 GiB resident budget with 8 GiB observed RSS reserves 24 GiB of future growth; resident memory is not subtracted twice and GPU budgets are not added to RAM.
The real Linux CPU child receives its address-space cap and is reaped when the simulated resident guard is exceeded; no model or large allocation used.
A real owned queued worker waits before tool launch, survives the old sixty-second recovery threshold, then exits on owner cancellation without running its tool.
Fourteen background requests leave two foreground queue places; the sixteen-request bound is enforced, with all native launchers held.
